The second review of 1.24.36's givens (wip commit ca62870 against 1.24.35 as released, 8cb3281), 2026-11-24.
A reviewer who wrote none of the change and did not read the first review's cases (givens_review_1236/, givens_1236.js,
code_checks_1236.js). Every verdict was written from what the question or circuit IS before Lantern was run on it.
Nothing under src/ or the existing tests was touched. (src/ is the same at HEAD c88534c as at ca62870.)

How to replay
  node tests/fixtures/givens_review2_1236/replay.js [path/to/lantern.inner.html] [--only <id regex>]
    Loads the page and 1.24.35 (git show 8cb3281, read into memory) side by side in jsdom, then:
      cases_fit.js    174 questions: what the model is shown (the given and its lines, or none and then 1.24.35's prompt
                      byte for byte)
      cases_sim.js     39 builds: each given as shown, built and run on the ladder Lantern draws (lib.sim: push buttons,
                      selectors, floats by level, a pressure switch with cut-in and cut-out, overloads tripped and reset,
                      on-delay timers), and the givens as a small model copies them (fence, no END, numbered lines,
                      a line changed as the question asks)
      cases_rules.js   30 builds: "stop PB1 all", and the fill on two nc floats -- where it acts (simulated) and where it
                      must not (the plan compared with 1.24.35's)
      cases_guard.js   17 saved model replies with MAKE CONTROL (bench_run*.json, liftstation_1230/run_35b.json), each
                      built by both versions for its own question
      cases_user.js    33 scenarios of the user's own givens, each on a fresh page (localStorage set first where needed)
  Run on ca62870 (run_ca62870.txt): 293 cases: 209 AGREE, 84 DISAGREE (high 37, medium 32, low 15).
  (On 1.24.35 the same replay gives 134 AGREE: it has no givens, so it says little; given only for completeness.)

SUMMARY
  The givens are right where they fit. Every given Lantern shows for a question it does fit was built and run, and every
  one works: the three-wire starter with 1 to 3 stations, e-stop and lights; forward/reverse with its interlock and the
  new "stop PB1 all"; two and three motors in sequence; the delayed start with its horn; the compressor with cut-in and
  cut-out; the one-float fill; the two-float fill (it holds in from the low float to the high one, through an overload
  trip and reset); the sump with its alarm light or horn. The fill-on-two-nc-floats rule never changed a circuit it
  should not (sump, duplex, fill-and-drain, two stops, three floats, mixed floats, alarm floats on lights, heater, a
  solenoid valve) and the 17 saved bench replies draw as on 1.24.35. Near misses that the given's own word lists know
  (HOA, star-delta, two-wire, jog, VFD, PLC, thermostat, floats, refrigeration, duplex) get 1.24.35's prompt byte for byte.
  What is still wrong is mostly the FIT: a given is shown for questions it does not surely fit, against rule 7.
    - The sequence given reads the order wrongly ("the pump must not start before the fan is on", "conveyor 1 must not
      run unless conveyor 2 is running") and invents a second machine of the first's kind when the other is not in its
      word list (heater, dust collector) or drops a third (feeder).
    - The delayed start shows Lantern's own "10 s" when the question says "five seconds", "half a minute" or "1 hour",
      reads "stops after 2 minutes" as the delay, and drops the first motor of "the pump starts 10 s after the fan".
    - The starter and reversing givens are shown for two motors, for loads with no motor (street lights, a kiln), for
      hold-to-run machines (hoist, winch, crane, elevator), and with a safety device asked for but missing (a guard
      door switch, end-of-travel limits).
    - The user's own givens match on two shared words, are never refused by anything, and outrank every given of
      Lantern's: a kept three-wire conveyor starter is shown for a reversing or star-delta question, a kept one-pump
      sump in place of the duplex example of a lift-station question and for a fill question, a kept fill for a sump.
    - One gap in the new fill rule: the two-float fill given with a stop button added (as "... with a stop button"
      asks) is drawn in series again and short-cycles.

==== HIGH ============================================================================================================

H1. The sequence given is shown the wrong way round, or for machines it does not have.
    Cases: F-sq-04, F-sq-05, F-sq-06, F-sq-14, F-sq-15.
    Seen:
      - "the pump must not start before the fan is on": coil M1 "pump starter", coil M2 M1 "fan starter" -- the fan is
        held by the pump. Right: M1 the fan, M2 the pump held by it.
      - "conveyor 1 must not run unless conveyor 2 is running" (downstream first, the usual conveyor practice): M1
        "conveyor 1", M2 M1 "conveyor 2". Right: conveyor 2 first, conveyor 1 held by it.
      - "the feeder can only start after the conveyor and the crusher are running": two coils, conveyor then crusher;
        the feeder is gone. Right: three machines with the feeder last, or no given.
      - "the heater must not start unless the fan is running" (airflow before heat): "fan 1" and "fan 2". "the conveyor
        must not start until the dust collector is running": "conveyor 1" and "conveyor 2". Right: a fan and a heater; a
        dust collector and a conveyor -- or no given.
    Why: seqNames (GIVENS_CONTROL, ~line 36983) takes the loads in the order named and looks for the one that runs first
    only after after/until/unless/while/when/once, never before "before" and never by a number ("conveyor 1 ... unless
    conveyor 2"); with one word from LOADS it numbers that word ("fan 1", "fan 2") though the question names another
    machine LOADS does not know; with three names it falls back to the first name twice.

H2. The delayed-start given shows a wrong time, or a wrong circuit.
    Cases: F-dl-03, F-dl-04, F-dl-05, F-dl-06, F-dl-07, F-dl-08.
    Seen:
      - "a five second warning horn", "starts after a delay of half a minute", "a delayed start of 1 hour": timer TR1
        "10 s" each time -- Lantern's default, written as if it were the question's. Right: 5 s, 30 s, 1 h, or no given.
      - "the fan starts after a delay and stops after 2 minutes": timer TR1 "2 min" as the START delay, and nothing
        stops the fan. Right: no given (an interval timer).
      - "the pump starts 10 seconds after the fan starts", "a time delay relay that starts a fan 30 seconds after the
        pump": one motor (the pump; the fan) after a start button -- the other motor is gone. Right: two motors, or no
        given.
    Why: delayOf (~line 37015) returns "10 s" when it finds no number with a unit, and DURS knows no hours or number
    words; the not-list catches "motor 2", "second motor" and "two motors" but not two machines named by kind.

H3. The starter and reversing givens are shown for what they do not fit.
    Cases: F-sn-20, F-sn-21, F-sn-22, F-sn-23, F-sn-24, F-sn-41, F-sn-42, F-sn-43, F-rv-05, F-rv-06, F-rv-07, F-rv-14,
    F-rv-15, F-rv-16.
    Seen:
      - two motors: "starts two motors together with one start button", "an exhaust fan and a supply fan", "a motor
        starter for a conveyor and a separate starter for a fan" -- one coil M1.
      - no motor: "a contactor with start and stop buttons for the street lights" -- coil M1 "motor contactor", a motor
        overload, and a green "run" pilot light (the street lights read as a pilot light); "a start/stop contactor
        circuit for a kiln" -- "motor contactor" with a motor overload.
      - hold-to-run machines: "a reversing starter for a hoist with up and down pendant buttons", "forward/reverse ...
        for a hoist", "... for a winch", "a reversing starter for a crane trolley", "a motor starter ... for an electric
        hoist" -- each start sealed in by the coil's holding contact. A hoist, winch or crane pendant is constant-
        pressure (the motion stops when the button is let go); a sealed-in hoist keeps lifting. "a motor starter for a
        freight elevator" -- a plain start/stop with none of an elevator's door interlocks or limits.
      - a safety device asked for and missing: "a saw that cannot start while the guard door is open" (no guard switch),
        "forward/reverse ... for a conveyor with limit switches at each end", "a gate with open and close limit
        switches" (no limits).
    Right: no given for each (the module's own rule: "a load with no motor" and "more than the given" get none).
    Why: the starter's asks accepts "contactor" with no load word (the load becomes "motor"); LIGHTW takes any "lights";
    neither not-list knows two machines, lighting loads other than "lighting", kilns, ovens, hoists, winches, cranes,
    elevators, guards or limit switches (the reversing not-list has no "limit").

H4. The fill and sump givens for questions that are not theirs.
    Cases: F-sn-28, F-cp-12, F-f2-05, F-sp-05.
    Seen:
      - "a start/stop circuit for a pump that fills a tank": the fill given (rank 2 beats the starter's 1) -- an on/off
        selector and a float in place of the start and stop buttons asked for; the pump then starts by itself.
      - "a booster pump to pump up the pressure tank using a pressure switch": the fill given, with a FLOAT "tank full"
        ("pump up" read as filling).
      - "a well pump filling a cistern with two floats: one in the cistern to stop it when full and one in the well to
        stop it when the well runs low": the two-float fill given -- the low float a START with a holding contact.
        The well's float is a dry-run cut-out; copied, the pump is held in with the well dry.
      - "a sump pump with an on float and an off float": the one-float sump given; the off float, and the holding in
        between, are gone (TWO_FLOATS knows "on and off", not "an on float and an off float").
    Right: none of these givens.

H5. The two-float fill given with a stop button added short-cycles again.
    Case: S-f2-stopbutton (and the given shown for F-f2-01 / "..., with a stop button").
    Seen: the given plus "stop PB1 M1" (what the question asks the model to add) is drawn with FS1 and FS2 in series:
    the pump stops as soon as the water rises past the low float and the tank never fills.
    Why: the new rule (AI_CONTROL ~line 34448) returns when the rung has any stop (r.stops.length). With an e-stop (in
    L1) or a run light it holds in (S-f2-estop, S-f2-light agree). Right: the floats' jobs held in beside a stop button
    too (a stop button and a stop float in series are both stops).

H6. The user's own givens are matched too loosely and outrank everything.
    Cases: U-17, U-18, U-19, U-20, U-30, U-31, U-32.
    Seen (each after one "Keep as my given"):
      - kept "Conveyor starter" (three-wire): shown for "a reversing starter control circuit for a conveyor" in place of
        Lantern's reversing given, and for "a star-delta conveyor starter control circuit" (1.24.35 had no block).
      - kept "Motor starter": shown for "a two-speed motor starter control circuit".
      - kept one-pump "Sump pump": shown for "a duplex sump pump control circuit with an alternating relay and a high
        water alarm" IN PLACE OF the duplex example (a 4-line single pump, no alternator; copied, it builds with no
        problem); and for "a pump that fills a tank with a float switch" (a float that closes on rise: copied, the pump
        runs while the tank is full).
      - kept "Tank fill pump" (two nc floats): shown for "a sump pump with a low float and a high float".
      - kept "Pump starter": shown for "a pump starter for a duplex lift station with an alternating relay" in place of
        the duplex example.
    Why: userGiven (GIVENS ~line 36732) matches when the title's words (two or more) are all in the question, or two
    thirds of the kept question's words are; no not-test, no askOnly, no check that the circuit is the same kind (one
    pump or two, fill or empty, one direction or two), and rank 10 beats every given of Lantern's. A pump station's
    question is only ever shown the user's own, so the loosest match lands exactly where Lantern withholds its own.
    Right: a kept circuit only for a question that asks for that circuit -- at least Lantern's own givens' refusals
    (their not-tests) applied to it, never above a Lantern given that fits better, and never a one-pump circuit for a
    duplex/station question.

==== MEDIUM ==========================================================================================================

M1. Lights read wrong. Cases: F-sn-29, F-sn-30, F-sn-31.
    "a pilot light that goes on when stopped" and "a light that goes on when the motor stops" get BOTH a green run
    light and a red stopped light (stateOf clears "comes on"/"turns on" but not "goes on", so its "on" is read as run).
    "red and green pilot lights" gets one red run light.

M2. The motor's voltage written as the control supply. Cases: F-sn-32, F-sn-33, F-sn-34, F-rv-12.
    "a motor starter for 460 V" -> supply "460 V AC"; "DOL ... 3-phase motor, 400 V, 50 Hz" -> "400 V AC"; "motor is 3
    phase 415V" -> "415 V AC"; the same for forward/reverse at 400 V 50 Hz. A lone voltage is taken as the control's
    unless a motor word stands AFTER it. Right: no supply line where the question does not say the control's.

M3. Stations missed. Cases: F-sn-37 ("start/stop from either end of the conveyor"), F-sn-38 ("two start buttons and two
    stop buttons" -- stations() only knows the order stop ... start). One station shown.

M4. "no e-stop needed" gets estop ES1 (F-sn-35): estop() does not read a "no".

M5. The given shown for a question that asks more than it (not a safety device): F-sn-25 (key switch), F-sn-26 (photo
    eye stop), F-sn-27 ("hand/auto" with a slash), F-sn-44 (zero speed switch), F-cp-05 (unloader solenoid), F-cp-06
    (high temperature cut-out), F-cp-07 (compressor with start and stop buttons: the given has a selector instead),
    F-sp-06 (sump low water cut-off), F-fl-06 (fill with a well low-water cut-out), F-fl-11 (electrode probes: a float
    shown), F-fl-15 (a float that CLOSES when the tank is full: the given's nc float shown).

M6. AI_PARTS splits one circuit into "parts" and the given is fitted to the first only. Cases: F-fl-07, F-sp-13.
    "a pump that fills a tank with a float, 24 V DC control, and a pump running light" -> parts ["... with a float",
    "Draw 24 V DC control, and a pump running light"]; the given has neither the supply nor the light (fitted to the
    whole question it has both). The split is AI_PARTS' (older); the given makes it a block to copy without them.

M7. The two-float fill: misses. Cases: F-f2-04, S-f2-topbottom, S-f2-upperlower, S-f2-noNc.
    "a fill pump with a low float and a high float" gets no given ("fill pump" is not in its asks). The fill rule does
    not read floats named "bottom"/"top" or "lower level"/"upper level": drawn in series, short-cycling. The given copied
    with both nc left out is drawn as written -- the pump runs only above the high float, the tank overflows -- and
    nothing questions it (the code check needs a cut word; the fill rule needs nc).

M8. The compressor given is shown for "a compressor with a pressure switch" (no "air"), but the code check is sure of
    the cut-out's way only for an air compressor (AIRQ): the given copied without nc is drawn normally open -- the
    compressor runs only above its cut-out -- and not sent back. Case: S-cp-04 (S-cp-03, with "air", is sent back).

M9. "stop PB1 all" is ignored when exactly one coil has a start: with "start PB2 M1" and a fan M2 on a selector, PB1 is
    drawn in M1's rung only and pressing it leaves the fan running. Case: A-07. (AI_CONTROL ~line 34355: only() finds
    the coil with a start first, and the all test comes after it.)

M10. "a motor that starts 10 s after power is applied" gets the delayed start with start and stop buttons (F-dl-09).

M11. User givens: U-21 -- a kept conveyor starter (green run light) is shown, coil "conveyor starter" and all, for "a
    start stop control circuit for a pump with a green run light" (5 of its 6 words are generic control words).
    U-33 -- the bench's make questions are built by aiAct.solve with Chat's system prompt (~line 31175), so a circuit
    the user kept on that page changes what the bench's make-control question is shown (a kept 4-line "Motor starter"
    replaces Lantern's given with its pilot light). A bench run on Adam's laptop after he keeps a given is no longer
    comparable with one before. (Whether the bench should ignore kept givens is Adam's to say.)

==== LOW =============================================================================================================

L1. Misses (no given where one fits): F-sn-39 "a direct on line starter control circuit"; F-fl-03 "keeps the tank
    full" (asks has "keep", not "keeps"); F-fl-04 "fills a water tower"; F-fl-10 "fill a cattle trough"; F-sp-11 "a
    bilge pump with a float switch"; U-28 a kept "Conveyor starter" not shown for "the conveyors starter" (no stemming).
L2. F-sn-36 "a light conveyor" gets a green run light. F-sn-40 "to IEC with K1, S1 stop and S2 start" gets the US tags.
L3. S-dl-02, S-rv-04: the delayed start's "overload OL1 M1 CR1" and the reversing "overload OL1 M1 M2" draw OL1's
    normally closed contact in two rungs -- an overload relay with two NC contacts, which a typical one is not (one NC,
    one NO). One contact drawn once does the same (in the run relay's rung; in the common line of both coils).
L4. The store: U-11 a stored entry whose lines hold END and a MAKE line is shown as stored (the prompt's block ends
    early and a second one starts) -- keep() refuses such lines but nothing checks them at load; U-12 non-string lines
    show "[object Object]" in the prompt (nothing throws; Chat's system prompt is built).
L5. U-23 an explanation question ("Explain how a conveyor starter control circuit works") is shown the user's kept
    circuit to "write as it stands" (Lantern's own givens refuse askOnly questions).
L6. U-24 a block written with numbered lines is kept and shown with the numbers ("1. stop PB1 M1").
L7. U-25 two different circuits kept in the same millisecond get the same id ("user-" + Date.now()): the second
    replaces the first in the session, and forgetting it removes both from the store.

==== WHAT AGREES =====================================================================================================
  - Every given as shown for a question it fits, built and simulated (S-st-01..05, S-rv-01..03, S-sq-01..02, S-dl-01,
    S-cp-01..02, S-fl-01, S-f2-01..02, S-sp-01..02): start latches, stops drop, overloads drop and reset leaves it off,
    lights follow, the interlock holds, sequence and timer behave, the pressure switch's cut-in/cut-out and the floats'
    levels are right, the two-float fill holds in between and stays off coming down.
  - The givens copied as a small model writes them: in a fence without END, numbered, reordered, labels unquoted,
    renamed on/off, empty/full, start/stop, with an e-stop, a light, a run relay (S-f2-*, S-dl-copy-fence,
    S-st-copy-labels). The air compressor copied without nc is sent back once with its nc line (S-cp-03).
  - Fitting that works (F-st-01..31): 1, 2 ("two locations", "both ends", "2 places", "local and remote"), 3 stations;
    "between two stations" (a conveyor's) left at one; the control voltage from a transformer, a coil, "24VDC", "230 V
    coil" beside a 415 V motor; light states before and after the light word (run/stopped, off when it runs, not
    running, red-run/green-stopped, a power or trip light left to the model, "no lights"); saw/press as verbs; pump room.
  - Forward/reverse, sequence, delayed start, compressor, fills and sump: their right fits (F-rv-01..04, 13; F-sq-01..03,
    09..13; F-dl-01, 02, 13..16; F-cp-01..03, 09, 10, 14; F-fl-01, 02, 12..14; F-f2-01..03, 08; F-sp-01..04, 10, 12).
  - Near misses get no given and 1.24.35's prompt byte for byte (F-sn-01..19, F-rv-08..11, F-sq-07, 08, 12, F-dl-10..12,
    F-cp-04, 08, 11, 13, F-fl-05, 08, 09, F-f2-06, 07, F-sp-07..09, 14, 15 -- duplex and lift stations included).
  - "stop ... all" (A-01..06, 08..12): ahead of every rung with no note; ALL in capitals no longer read as a device;
    quoted "stop all" a label; the duplex keeps its wiring.
  - The fill rule (R-01..04, 10..23): holds a make-up pump in; leaves a pressure cut-out in series; never makes a low
    suction or dry-run cut-out a start (the code check sends them back first); leaves sump, duplex, two stops, three
    floats, fill-and-drain, two stop floats, mixed nc/no, alarm floats, the 1.24.34 emptying rule, "pump out", a start
    button, a heater and a solenoid valve as 1.24.35 drew them.
  - The 17 saved replies (G-*) draw as on 1.24.35.
  - The user's givens: Keep shown under a clean control circuit only (not with problems, not electronics); kept as the
    AI wrote it with the question; the same and a reworded question shown it, once, in place of Lantern's; Forget it
    clears store, session and prompt and turns the button back; loaded at start; a store that is not JSON, an object or
    an array of junk changes nothing; the same block kept twice stored once; 50 kept at most; the day and the practice
    (US, IEC) said; a kept duplex shown for its station question; a kept compressor above Lantern's (U-01..10, 13..16,
    22, 26, 27, 29).

==== WHAT WAS NOT RUN ================================================================================================
  - No model: nothing here says what a 0.8B, 2B, 4B or the 35B writes when shown these givens; "a small model copies it"
    is CLAUDE.md's lesson, not a run.
  - No browser: the ladders were checked as plans and simulated, not drawn in Chromium; the view's buttons were clicked
    in jsdom through aiAct.view, not in a Chat turn.
  - The code checks' own review (US/IEC choice, the references) is another reviewer's; only where they touch the
    givens (S-cp-02..04, R-03, R-04, U-27) were they run.
  - Outside the change, seen on the way: AI_CONTROL's own match does not know "3-wire control" (F-sn-19 asks a control
    circuit and gets no control instructions at all, as on 1.24.35); the pre-start horn with no time said is shown
    Lantern's "10 s" (F-dl-15, agreed: a default, but it is a time Lantern chose).
